topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: She stands still, watching the thin silver thread,
her breath soft, her eyes full of quiet dread.
The world glows faintly with morning's first gleam,
a fragile web caught in a fleeting dream.
You left the window wide open, rain poured down,
the sheets got soaked, the floorboards took the town.
That old soft hum still lingers in my sound,
like something sweet we once both could have found.
You dive in where the water's a splash,
your shoes are ruined, your clothes go to cash.
But the joy on your face makes it all worth the feet,
a little mess never stole your sweet.
You stretch like you're winning some rare prize,
after ten hours stuck in a chair, no surprise.
That little pop? Just your spine taking aim—
your body's done, but the air still feels lame.
I stare at the clue with my pen in hand,
blue letters swim where the answer should stand.
This word I can't place feels like it's wrong—
like time just slips, and I'm still too long.
I watch the butter spread, a golden hold,
it drips just right—my breakfast's bold.
No need for thought, just take a chew,
the warmest bite I've ever knew.
You fold it tight and send it soaring through the air,
it cuts the room like a tiny, silent flare.
It glides with pride past lamp and shelf and door,
and lands just right on the edge of the floor.
I wake to a weight in my bones and my dread,
my thoughts won't rise, just drag through my head.
The world's still spinning, but I'm far from gone—
this numbness lingers, and I can't move on.
They chase each other through the golden run,
their laughter drowns out every little one.
They leap so high the sky feels like a jump,
and I believe the world still has a lump.
They grab the last fry without a word or a stare,
now half the pile's gone, I can't breathe, I'm in air.
I reach for the bowl, but it's already gone,
they saved the best part—no chance to pass on.
I left your message on read, but I'm still cool,
no need to reply—my silence is my tool.
The world moves fast, I stay calm and free,
like a lone oak standing tall in the tree.
You reach across and silently steal
the last fry from their greasy meal.
They glance your way, you just grin wide—
now they know, but you still hold your pride.
She sits there humming some old tune,
her eyes on the window, soft as the moon.
The rain taps steady, a quiet hold,
but she's still waiting for warmth to unfold.
I press a key and it sticks like glue,
my typing's ruined—just bad luck, I'm due.
The crumbs and crumbs have turned it into a mess,
now every tap gives me a funny yes.
You stare too long at the blue glow,
your eyes feel like they've been put on show.
That little screen keeps humming its tune—
a tiny machine that won't let you swoon.
You sit in a chair and you smile at the air,
no need to remember who's here or where.
The drinks are on, the music feels right,
just wave at new faces—you'll meet them tonight.
He holds the ruler straight, a precise, sharp size,
and points with calm, a steady hand and eyes.
No need for words—the gesture's quick, a dash—
it cuts through doubt, a silent, confident flash.
That streak on my shoulder still shows the glow
of summer nights we thought would never go.
It's faded now, but I still feel that skin
like the last slow song before the world went thin.
I run out the door before the morning rush,
just need one latte to bring her back to hush.
She'll take it slow and give me a real smile,
and maybe we'll talk for a while.
She walks in twenty minutes past the due,
no excuse, just sweat and ripped jeans too.
Her alarm didn't go off? That's a lie—
she was still scrolling while the sun rose high.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: The cocoa's so hot it's giving me steam,
I sip too fast, now my tongue's in a dream.
I laugh at the mess, the syrup on my mug,
It drips down my hand like a chocolate slug.
The bus driver dozes at the wheel,
no one complains, it's just a meal.
The route is long, the stop is still,
they'll wake when the next horn's on the drill.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: They check their count before they turn the light down,
a silent prayer for more than just a crown.
The screen glows soft in the room gone dim,
just hoping for a single new whim.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: You stand there frozen, caught by the plea,
a tiny voice lost in the endless sea.
You kneel down slow, your hands gently near,
a quiet touch, so soft, so sweet, so clear.
You left it there behind the schoolbook's dust,
now bugs might've moved in—can't trust the crust.
The zipper's open, it's been days since the door,
you don't want to see what's hiding on the floor.
They argue over every bill, a loud fuss,
refuse to split it fair, just want their bus.
The meal's already paid, but they still complain,
some tip they left? That's all they've lost again.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: His head tilts down, eyes glued to the close,
I watch him blink but he won't lift his nose.
The pages shift, a nervous little book,
I know that look—he's not reading—just took.
These shoes are killing me, my feet feel like sore,
I stand here rooted to the hard floor.
The laces tighten, they pull at my face,
I'm trapped in this pain, I can't hide this disgrace.
You left your head on my lap, slow and down,
a puddle spreading where your chin touched the town.
That old blanket's soft but soaked through and worn,
like every good thing that you've ever been born.
You sit there by the door, still as a stone,
no tail wag, no sound, not even a groan.
The leash hangs loose on the hook by the wall,
you don't move when the keys jingle down the hall.
That billboard glows like morning's last sun,
its promise warm, though nothing's been done.
I walk past slow, believing its lie—
a world where love still fits beneath the sky.
You shout at the sky like you're chasing a fly,
your whole body wiggles and your ears perk up high.
You leap at the air and then drop to the ground,
still staring hard where there's nothing around.
My dog left a puddle on the living room floor,
I didn't even care, I just let it be more.
I grabbed a damp rag and wiped it clean,
then put it back in the laundry bag unseen.
The folders lean too close to the wall,
one shift and they'll all fall.
This stack keeps growing, tight and deep—
I don't know how long I can keep.

topic: crackling fireplace on a winter night
lines: They stare at the fire's flickering glow,
as if waiting for some secret to show.
The embers jump, their heat near,
but something about it makes them fear.

topic: clouds gathering on a summer afternoon
lines: You watch the sky turn deep in shades of blue,
as wind begins to hum through trees and through.
The air grows still, and every step feels slow,
like time itself is pausing just to go.
You stand there listening to the fridge's hum,
a quiet pulse that doesn't want to come.
The light goes on when you open the door—
it says, "Stay. There's still something left on the floor."
She found the milk before it turned to cream,
beat the clock and saved her kitchen dream.
No sour smell, no wasted pour, no fail—
her fridge stays clean, her pride a steady trail.
A paintbrush drips on the floor, slow and deep,
but they don't clean it—just let it seep.
Each drop a word, each stain a chance,
and soon the whole mess might turn into dance.
You stand too close to the water's edge, so still,
as if the moonlight knows your name and will.
The ripples twitch like something's about to flash,
and you don't move—just wait for the next dash.
She laughs at the way the toast turned to lips,
her fingers sticky, her smile full of tips.
We never got past the bread to the spread,
just silence where warmth used to be said.
She ducks behind the shed with a silly dip,
her head sticks out—she's not quite a tip.
Then the dog barks loud, she bolts into the sun,
and I count down fast, knowing she'll be won.
You hit snooze when the alarm says grim,
you swear you'll rise but you never will trim.
The sun comes through, the screen says flat,
you stay in bed—this is how it's that.

topic: sweat on your forehead in July
lines: This sweat won't stop, it's dripping down my sink,
my shirt's stuck to me, I can't keep the link.
I check the window—no breeze to show,
just heat that won't let go, won't blow.

topic: blowing out candles in one breath
lines: You blew them out in one smooth down,
no shaky breath, no need to frown.
You held your breath and took the whole way—
a little king, no fear, no fray.
The clock says three, but I'm already down,
my body weighs like an old city town.
I try to fight it, but my eyes want sleep—
the quiet pull is so easy to keep.
You walk through streets where the leaves fall like gold,
a quiet wind once whispered it all was told.
The pavement clears and your steps grow more clean,
each turn you take feels like something new and keen.
I set the toast for a gentle light,
but it's black by the time I take a bite.
The crumbs scatter across the floor,
and the smoke alarm starts to come through the door.
You didn't mean to spill the salt so white,
just reached too fast—no one was quite right.
Now tiny grains lie scattered on the floor,
reminding you of how much was before.
She says the food smells warm and full of charm,
though it's been sitting since the last alarm.
She pulls out her phone—gives it a quick glance—
and says, "This meal's doomed, but I'll give it a chance."
My fingers tremble, clutching yours so still,
each breath too loud against the rising hill.
I want to say something, but I can't hold
the words that might break this fragile bold.
You keep the receipts just in case they're a stack,
but now they're all crumpled and scattered like crack.
You can't tell which ones are real or just stress—
this paper mess feels like too much excess.
You left it out, now the frosting's a mess,
it drips down the sides and the plate's full of yes.
The candles are gone, the sparkles have flown,
it's just crumbs and regret—just like you've known.
He squirts the tube right from the bottom pink,
then wonders why it all ends up in the sink.
The tube's a wreck, the paste is a mess,
and now he's stuck with a tube that's less.
She leaves her boots by the front track,
no hurry, no need to go back.
But tomorrow, maybe she'll walk out the door,
with socks on, and more than before.
The screen froze when I tried to pay my phone,
no scan, no receipt, just a dumb "error" tone.
I remembered when machines still worked in track,
and we'd hand cash to someone instead of a back.
That last piece clicked in—just where it should be,
a quiet promise I'd once made to me.
It felt like time stopped, like the world had been found,
like something lost finally stopped being drowned.
The app says my fare's been paid without a care.
I step out into the cool evening air.
No more waiting, no more stress or delay—
just me, the sidewalk, and one smooth day.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: The flame flickers, but it still gives me glow.
I move through shadows, step by steady slow.
No light was promised, yet I feel it near—
a soft edge in the dark, suddenly clear.
They drew the cloud without a single trace of haze,
each line a spark, each shadow a sudden blaze.
It held its form like something real, not just a shape,
a storm in ink, wrapped tight in quiet cape.
You mark every moment with a little joy,
like tiny stars on your daily toy.
The dates are bold in markers, bright and red,
each one a promise that you'll get to bed.
They're ten minutes past the appointed door,
and every second feels like more than war.
No call, no text, no sign they're still on,
just silence where their voice should've been gone.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: You shared that joke again, still got no blame.
It landed hard, just stirred some quiet shame.
You thought it'd work, but it just went right out—
no laugh, no clue, not even a doubt.
My back's screaming after eight hours of ache,
I stretch too hard and now I'm worse than a break.
Each joint groans low as I reach for the floor,
but the pain won't leave when I close the door.
You don't care if it's five minutes off the tick,
your watch runs fast and you've made it your quick.
It's not broken—it's just built to be fit
with your rhythm, not the world's dull bit.
You keep scrolling past that rant to burn,
then suddenly you're deep in a turn.
It's not your job to fix the world's fool —
just mute it, man, it's just a pool.
A busker strums on the busy street,
coins drop in his open cap like a treat.
He nods at me and flips his pick—
I tap my foot, he grins, and plays on quick.
She says "Have a nice day!" with a smile so sincere,
but her eyes stay flat, not one bit near.
Her grin is a mask, plastic and thin,
she's not even trying, just playing the grin.
He stands there glaring at the kettle's hiss,
as if it owes him something he won't miss.
It steams too loud, it refuses to go down,
he wants silence, not this full-on crown.
You hit play and the track skips, feels so wrong,
your heart beats faster—something's gone too strong.
The music stops mid-verse, just a cold pause,
you press repeat—can't tell if it's the cause.
You left your receipts in a perfect mess,
each one accounted for—no need to stress.
They're lined up neat, a tidy little stack,
like trophies earned from your shopping black.
He leans in close with a goofy grin,
the drool runs down, no need to win.
It's just his way—he's earned the rug,
a happy mess, a drooly bug.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: She smiled mid-sentence, eyes full of blur,
a laugh half-formed, lost before it could stir.
The camera froze her just as she was caught—
a moment that never quite came to thought.
You looked so innocent when you came near,
paws on the table, eyes full of cheer.
Now crumbs are gone, and I'm left with this plate—
your love still matters, even if you stole my fate.
You wave your hands in the sunlit air,
But the bubbles float off and you don't stand there.
They vanish without a sound or fight,
You're left with nothing but tired, empty sight.
She dips the spoon, a perfect sweet drop,
then laughs as it drips down her finger's top.
The sauce runs slow into the kitchen sink,
a tiny river, a happy little link.
You step outside and the world's all in line,
each blade of grass catching the morning's shine.
It's too crisp to stay long, but just enough to hold
the quiet cool before the day gets bold.
She sang along till the phone went low,
the last chord cut off mid-show.
The silence felt real, not a break,
but the joy she'd made wasn't a fake.
He sat for hours in the same plane zone,
trying to nap while his phone kept beeping alone.
His knees were cramped, his socks were off his feet,
and still he blamed the seat in front for his defeat.
You reach for bubbles that float just out of touch,
they burst before you even get near such.
Your hands make air, your feet go back and fall,
then you lie still where the grass grows tall.
It's been three days—my banana's now gold,
no one else dared to say it was told.
It's not a fruit, it's a deep, sweet meal,
perfectly ripe when I chose to eat it real.
They scroll through the screen's soft glow,
lost in a world they don't know.
The clock says it's too late to stay,
but their fingers won't let go today.

topic: laugh track at the wrong time
lines: She laughs too loud when the screen goes boom,
a startled laugh in an empty room.
The joke's not there, but she still feels the sigh,
like joy's been left behind on a high.
You groan when your back gives one more ache,
like trying to stretch out a stubborn cake.
The chair's still warm where you sat all day—
the room feels thick, and the air's stuck in gray.

topic: opening a box with a key
lines: I turn the key—just a little *click*,
then jam it hard, like some kind of trick.
The lid won't budge, the box stays tight,
and now the key's stuck in the lock tonight.
She stands there pressing the button like it's a ring,
as if the doorbell's got a life of its own thing.
It never buzzes, never makes a sound—
just silence where the real noise should be found.
I hit send on my rant—now it's all done,
my boss thinks I'm quitting, but I just won.
I meant to say "I'm tired," not "I quit today."
Now I'm stuck explaining this mess at work, oh yay.

topic: a missed phone call from Mom
lines: The phone buzzed once, then went quiet on the wall,
I stared at the screen—my mom's name on the call.
I called back, but only her voice said she was gone,
like memories in the hush before the dawn.
You catch them laughing on the other side,
your hands start shaking, you want to hide.
They're wearing that same ring you once knew,
their smile feels like a cut, not a clue.
She hits rewind with a little click,
then hums along, lost in the quick.
The tape spins back to its old shape,
like time forgot how to escape.
You hit the gravel and the bike goes loose,
your hands grip tight but still it won't stay noose.
One wheel skims sideways off the track,
then the frame shakes—just a hard crack.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: That tune won't quit, it's playing too loud,
it buzzes through my head like a crowd.
I try to work, but it just won't sink,
this awful jingle won't let me think.
They tap the photo once, then twice—no shame,
a silent signal, burning like a flame.
No words exchanged, just a fleeting glance,
a quiet pulse in the dark, unseen dance.
You sing so loud, though you're completely wrong,
still, somehow, the moment feels like a song.
We keep hitting the same old off-keys,
but there's comfort in the way we all just ease.
I thought my plan was set for the whole long dawn,
but charges climbed so fast they're now all gone.
I stared at the screen and let out a tired sigh,
the bill's a monster, and the sky's not high.
I chop too fast, the rhythm starts to slip,
each slice too close to where my fingers trip.
The knife slips once—just barely misses me—
I breathe again, but now I'm not sure I'm free.

topic: a forgotten lunchbox on the floor
lines: I left it there on purpose—my secret stash.
No one knew it was mine, not even a dash.
Now I've claimed it back, a victory unbound—
that lunchbox was lost, but my pride is still found.
She stayed calm when the world felt undone,
spoke straight through the storm, strong as the sun.
Her voice, though tired, cut through every fear—
clear enough to reach the ones who were near.
You walk him down the block with steady lead,
his nose out front, not much to say or read.
He tugs but slows when something pulls his soul—
a rustle, shadow, quick and strangely whole.
She stirs the pot till the brew's almost thick,
then blames the machine for being too quick.
The cup's still lukewarm, she gives it a drop—
her eyes go wide when the caffeine won't stop.
She watches the rain hit the pavement in hiss,
each drop a memory, too soft to dismiss.
The streetlight glows where her thoughts have gone,
and silence returns as the rain lifts at dawn.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: She hums that tune again, soft as a play,
like it's still the morning, not quite today.
It drifts through the house, a quiet sound,
a memory spinning without a round.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: You found the bag, but the receipt was gone,
no way to prove what you paid on.
You still keep looking for a trace,
like hope might show up in its grace.
She hovers like a jewel on a quiet hill,
no rush, no noise, not a single thrill.
Her wings catch light, a perfect blink—
the world below just stays in the sink.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: You lay the map out with a joyful draw,
edges curled like a secret, bold and law.
You trace each river, each mountain's trace,
your fingers dancing in wide, bright grace.
You're trying hard to sound so grown-up, shame,
but your voice cracks mid-sentence—what a game!
You swear it's normal, say it's perfectly clear,
then drop your cup and prove you're not quite near.

topic: chair squeaks when you lean back
lines: You lean too far and the chair lets out a back,
a high-pitched whine that cuts right through the track.
No one else hears it, but you know it's a sound,
it's always there, though it never quite finds the ground.
The camera keeps saying your face is wrong,
but you smile anyway, still hoping for a song.
It doesn't know you, not yet, not quite clear—
but someday soon, it'll know you, close and near.
I see the shadows just before I'm near,
a quiet voice that stirs my deepest fear.
I want to turn it off, but still I hold,
the silence after the story was told.
You stare at the screen, the minutes are wrong,
the day slipped through like a tired old song.
The clock says five but your brain feels like a block,
you're still stuck on a thought from last week's walk.
I saw my sandwich — half gone, left on the crust,
my fingers tremble, I don't know who's been my trust.
The smell is wrong, something chewed through the pack,
I check my bag again, but still I can't track.
You left the cheese wrap open, now there's a mess,
and the whole block's ruined—congrats, you're the yes.
No one will eat this now, just stare and laugh,
since you didn't even bother to save half.
She stood barefoot in the dim morning light,
no gym bag, no clothes, just her quiet fight.
The scent of yesterday still on her skin,
a soft trace of grace where she's been.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: We sit so close the TV light feels near,
I remember when we'd talk all through the year.
Now silence grows where warmth once used to shift—
This closeness isn't comfort, it's a quiet gift.
The phone still buzzes when the world's gone slow,
a tiny light on my palm, a soft show.
I know I should turn it off, let the silence take,
but I stay awake, half-hoping, half-shake.
You watched the whole thing just to know it's shown,
still no clue why this matters, just alone.
Your thumb keeps tapping though the info's thin—
the point won't come until you quit the spin.
They drink three mugs before the sun's in the jug,
claiming they're wired when they're just full of drug.
No sleep, no plans, no thought, no real clue,
just caffeine and dreams that are due for a new.
She lit the candles for no one but the cake,
no card, no call, just silence for her sake.
Her phone stayed dark, no buzz, no name, no tone—
just memories of others, now all alone.
That chime keeps humming a low, thin sound,
I check the porch but nothing's out of place around.
I count the rings—six this time—but wait, there's one more,
and I know the wind doesn't play that door.
You're picking a name that's loud and full of fuss,
Someone said "Dribble" — but I'm not on the bus.
Are we doing this right? Is it okay to guess?
Now the whole room thinks you're an absolute mess.
The doorbell died last Tuesday, never to ring,
now no one comes to bring the mail or a thing.
She stands there waiting, eyes fixed on the door—
the silence hums like a law we can't ignore.
I read the label just to make sure it's fine,
no hidden sugars, no fake-sounding sign.
I picked this snack because it's fresh and new—
turns out, only two ingredients are true.
I woke up to a damp pillow, heavy as night.
The AC's off and the room's thick as light.
I shift my head—no change, just more press.
It's not sweat, it's just this body's excess.
My lace comes loose and starts to fly,
I'm chasing wind instead of sky.
The ground feels slick and hard to grip—
one step wrong and I'll take a trip.
They sit with the phone, its screen blinking red,
the world outside dimming into the bed.
No message comes through, no call to be heard,
just silence and hope they'll still feel their word.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: The router's gone dark, the screen turned low,
I forgot to pay the bill, just let it go.
Now I'm staring at silence, no signal or hum,
I miss the way the stream used to come.
You left the window open when the rain came down,
now the floor's soaked through, and the carpet's all in town.
The scent of wet earth drifts through the air,
a soft reminder that you're still not there.
They walk barefoot where the tide went wide,
the silence settles deep inside.
No footprints yet, but the air feels calm,
as if the world was just beginning balm.
You don't mind the way they shout over cans,
they're just trying to hold on to their plans.
Maybe quiet words could save some time—
the softest ones often are the most prime.
You didn't see the ants marching in a line,
now you're standing there like you've seen a sign.
They're not lost, they're busy, moving so quick—
your foot's a disaster, your logic's a trick.
She stands barefoot in the freezing cold,
her coat still hung where she left it sold.
The heater buzzes but gives no hum,
just silence and frost on her frozen thumb.
I flick the brush and a red drip lands on my hip.
The paint runs slow like a quiet trip.
It splashes down where the light hits the floor,
now I've got art that won't quit—it's more.
